from.place: the provisional RelativeProj proof sentence: “every piece is a direct summand of the quasi-coherent underlying module, hence quasi-coherent. On an affine open the equivalence with modules preserves coproducts. Apply sections to decomposition; the resulting map from the direct sum is bijective. The inclusions are injective, so replacing each piece by its image gives this internal sum.”

title: On an affine open the homogeneous section subgroups are an internal direct sum.
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $\mathcal A$ be a quasi-coherent commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebra sheaf [def-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra] [def-weil-pbc-comm-algebra-sheaf]. Let $(B_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ be sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] equipped with a commutative unital graded sheaf algebra structure [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures], and let $d:\bigoplus_{n\ge0}B_n\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal A$ be a specified isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules from the coproduct of the $B_n$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] to the underlying module of $\mathcal A$, respecting the multiplication and the unit. Write $i_n:B_n\to\mathcal A$ for the composite of the $n$th coproduct inclusion with $d$. For an affine open $V\subseteq X$, put $C_V=\Gamma(V,\mathcal A)$ and let $C_{V,n}=\operatorname{im}(i_n(V):\Gamma(V,B_n)\to C_V)$, an additive subgroup of $C_V$. Then $C_V$ is the internal direct sum of the $C_{V,n}$: the additive map from the group $\bigoplus_{n\ge0}C_{V,n}$ of finitely supported families $(c_n)_n$ with $c_n\in C_{V,n}$ to $C_V$, $(c_n)_n\mapsto\sum_n c_n$, is bijective; equivalently every $c\in C_V$ is uniquely a finite sum $\sum_n c_n$ with $c_n\in C_{V,n}$. These are the section ring and image subgroups denoted by $A.\mathrm{sections}(V)$ and $A.\mathrm{sectionGrade}(V,n)$ for the given relative Proj input algebra $A$, and the conclusion is $\mathrm{DirectSum.IsInternal}(A.\mathrm{sectionGrade}(V))$.

proof.text: Transport the coproduct projections through decomposition. Composing a homogeneous inclusion with its own projection and reinclusion is the inclusion; composing with a different projection is zero. Thus the homogeneous projections extract the coordinates of the additive recomposition homomorphism. By direct-sum induction, recomposition is injective.

For the coproduct of underlying abelian sheaves, the map from the presheaf coproduct to the total algebra sheaf factors through sheafification by an epimorphism: cancellation can be tested on all summand inclusions using the coproduct universal property. Sheaf epimorphisms and the sheafification unit are locally surjective. Evaluation of the presheaf coproduct is an abelian-group coproduct, whose elements are finite sums. Consequently every section is locally a finite sum of homogeneous inclusions.

For a section over an affine open, select a finite subcover of these local presentations using compactness of the affine open. Let S be the finite union of their degree sets. On each selected open, orthogonality shows the sum over S of the homogeneous projections equals the original section. Sheaf separation makes that equality global. A finite sum of direct-sum generators therefore maps to the given section, proving surjectivity. These arguments also apply to the empty affine open.
